case_prompt:
A 78-year-old woman presented with acute vision loss and headache. Her ocular history was notable for pseudophakia in both eyes, dry macular degeneration, and open-angle glaucoma treated chronically with latanoprost 0.005% nightly in both eyes; three weeks earlier she was started on Simbrinza™ (brimonidine 0.1%/brinzolamide 0.1%) twice daily in both eyes. She also had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

On examination, visual acuity was 20/400 in the right eye and 20/200 in the left eye. Pupils were equally reactive without a relative afferent pupillary defect. Intraocular pressures were 24 mm Hg OD and 23 mm Hg OS. Slit-lamp examination revealed quiet anterior chambers that were shallow in the periphery. Indentation gonioscopy showed closed angles in both eyes. Ultrasound biomicroscopy demonstrated iridocorneal apposition with 360° choroidal effusions in both eyes. Manifest refraction revealed a myopic shift of 3 diopters in each eye.

Her ocular history was notable for pseudophakia in both eyes, dry macular degeneration, and open-angle glaucoma treated chronically with latanoprost 0.005% nightly in both eyes; three weeks earlier she was started on Simbrinza™ (brimonidine 0.1%/brinzolamide 0.1%) twice daily in both eyes.

On examination, visual acuity was 20/400 in the right eye and 20/200 in the left eye.
Pupils were equally reactive without a relative afferent pupillary defect.
Intraocular pressures were 24 mm Hg OD and 23 mm Hg OS.
Slit-lamp examination revealed quiet anterior chambers that were shallow in the periphery.

diagnostic_reasoning: 1. Brinzolamide–induced effusions were considered given its sulfamate moiety similar to topiramate and acetazolamide — “we initially hypothesized the choroidal effusions were due to brinzolamide … and therefore, has the potential to cause this idiosyncratic reaction.” 2. Latanoprost was also considered for its ability to increase uveoscleral outflow and disrupt the blood-aqueous barrier in pseudophakic eyes — “Latanoprost increases aqueous flow into [the] uveoscleral outflow pathway and could disrupt blood-aqueous barrier in pseudophakic eyes.”

selection.screen_reason: Bilateral angle closure with choroidal effusions and myopic shift three weeks after starting a sulfonamide-containing eye drop in pseudophakic eyes.
selection.second_look_note: Starting brimonidine-brinzolamide drops three weeks earlier is the key history clue to bilateral angle closure with choroidal effusions.
